To determine who was allowed to participate in the Greek democratic process during the time period of the text (Classical Athens in the 5th century B.C.E., as described by Thucydides in Pericles' Funeral Oration):

1. **Analyze historical context:** The passage describes Athenian democracy. In ancient Athens, democracy was direct, but political participation (voting in the Assembly, holding office, serving on juries) was strictly limited.
2. **Determine gender restrictions:** Women were entirely excluded from the political process and were not considered citizens with voting rights. This eliminates options (B) and (D).
3. **Determine citizenship/birth restrictions:** Political participation was limited to adult males who were citizens. Furthermore, under the citizenship law introduced by Pericles in 451/0 B.C.E., an Athenian citizen had to be born of a legally married Athenian mother and father (citizens of the state by birth). 
4. **Evaluate remaining options:** Option (A) ("All adult men born within the geographic boundaries of the state") is too broad because it would include slaves, resident aliens (metics), and children of foreigners born in Athens. Option (C) ("All adult men who were citizens of the state by birth") accurately reflects the exclusive definition of Athenian political participants.

Final answer: C
